guides.title: Overview: capabilities and roles
guides.audience: Everyone: sponsors, architects, administrators and developers
guides.purpose: What EA Explorer is, what it does, how it follows the TOGAF Standard, and who does what in it: the kinds of people who use it, the roles they hold and what each role may do. Read it first; every other guide builds on it.

guides.title: System architecture and platform developer guide
guides.audience: Platform developers who change EA Explorer itself, and architects who review how it is built
guides.purpose: How EA Explorer is built (its containers, services, databases and code layout) and how a developer gets the code, runs it, changes it, tests it and releases it.

guides.title: Install guide
guides.audience: System administrators installing EA Explorer on a laptop or a server
guides.purpose: Everything needed to put EA Explorer on a machine and have it running: the choices (laptop, server, your own database), the machine to prepare, the installation itself, your certificate on the front door, and the first-run setup.

guides.title: System administrator guide
guides.audience: Super Admins, IT Admins and User Admins
guides.purpose: Running the installation: people and their roles, security, settings, branding, machine access and the system's own configuration, with a step-by-step How do I for every task.

guides.title: Day-to-day operations guide
guides.audience: IT Admins and Super Admins who keep EA Explorer running
guides.purpose: The everyday work of keeping EA Explorer healthy: starting and stopping, health and alerts, logs, backups, the job queue, the command centre and schedules, with a step-by-step How do I for each task.

guides.title: Tuning and optimisation guide
guides.audience: IT Admins and Super Admins sizing and tuning an installation
guides.purpose: Sizing a new installation, measuring how it runs, the optimisation report and its suggestions, more API and job servers, scaling out, and keeping the databases in good order.

guides.title: Administrator guide for models
guides.audience: Model Admins
guides.purpose: Looking after models: creating them, their metamodels, who may work on them, versions, tags and merging, data quality, and the model wizards, with a step-by-step How do I for each task.

guides.title: Administrator guide for projects
guides.audience: Project Admins
guides.purpose: Setting up and running architecture projects: kinds of projects, templates and bases, the ADM cycle, charters, people, governance, deliverables and sign-off, surveys and maturity, with a step-by-step How do I for each task.

guides.title: Architects' guide
guides.audience: Practising architects
guides.purpose: The everyday work of an architect in EA Explorer: finding and changing content, committing it, views and reports, bringing data in and taking it out, stakeholders and key questions, and working in projects, with a step-by-step How do I for each task.

guides.title: Industry expert guide: making an industry model
guides.audience: Industry modellers who build reference models for an industry
guides.purpose: How to make an industry model: the metamodel, building it in Excel, the industry packs, and publishing it as a reference model in the library, with a step-by-step How do I for each task.

guides.title: Developer guide: connectors and integrations
guides.audience: Developers who write ETLs, scripts, connectors and reports against EA Explorer
guides.purpose: Everything a developer can build against EA Explorer, with examples: authentication, the REST API, push sources and the Python kit, deliveries, OData feeds and sources, webhooks, import formats and MCP.

guides.title: Disaster recovery guide
guides.audience: Super Admins and IT Admins responsible for recovery
guides.purpose: Getting EA Explorer back after a failure: backups or DR and which to use, the DR pack, rebuilding on another machine, the restores from one model to everything, and what to do first in a catastrophe.

guides.title: Site pairing for hot-standby DR
guides.audience: Super Admins setting up a second site
guides.purpose: Pairing two EA Explorer sites so that a DR site is kept read only and up to date with the primary (hot standby), ready to take over; and content sync between sites. Pairing is one way: the DR site takes over with Stop and take over, it does not take changes at the same time as the primary.

guides.title: Emergency guide
guides.audience: Super Admins and IT Admins, when something urgent has gone wrong
guides.purpose: What to do when you cannot get in or a secret must change now: resetting an administrator's password, unlocking, removing a lost authenticator, break-glass sign-in, and rotating passwords, keys and certificates.

guides.title: EAX command guide
guides.audience: Anyone who runs EA Explorer from the machine
guides.purpose: The eax command, in full: how it is used, what each group of commands does, and every command with its options and examples, as `eax help` gives them.

guides.title: Jenkins guide
guides.audience: Super Admins and IT Admins who run eax commands from Jenkins
guides.purpose: Jenkins beside EA Explorer: a pipeline for every eax command and DR tool, run with a click; how to start it, sign in, run a pipeline and look after it.

guides.title: An example project, end to end
guides.audience: Architects and Project Admins learning EA Explorer
guides.purpose: One architecture project followed from start to finish in EA Explorer, using the sample project Protea Claims Transformation 2028 that comes with the demo data: setting it up, the charter, stakeholders and key questions, the ADM phases, gaps and the migration plan, deliverables and sign-off, and finishing.

guides.title: Guide to testing the installation
guides.audience: IT Admins and Super Admins checking an installation works
guides.purpose: Testing an installation from the inside and from outside: the self-test and its suites, watching a test, reading the results, cleaning up, and the test bench.

guides.title: Guide to testing backup and DR
guides.audience: Super Admins and IT Admins proving that backups and DR work
guides.purpose: Proving that backups restore and that DR works, both by hand and with the commands: checking a backup, the restore drill, the monthly drill, the new-machine drill and eax-drill.

guides.title: Upgrade guide
guides.audience: Super Admins and IT Admins upgrading EA Explorer
guides.purpose: Upgrading EA Explorer, either directly from a release on git (Updates, or eax update) or by getting the latest code by hand and upgrading; choosing channels, and rolling an update back.

guides.title: Troubleshooting guide for administrators
guides.audience: IT Admins and Super Admins finding out what is wrong
guides.purpose: Finding out what is wrong and putting it right: status, logs and diagnostics, health and alerts, failing checks, containers, jobs and the database, and every error code with what to do.

guides.title: AI and MCP user guide
guides.audience: Everyone who works with EA Explorer through an AI assistant
guides.purpose: Working with EA Explorer through your AI assistant: connecting it, what it can do for each kind of user, and the MCP server and its tools.

guides.title: Setting up Keycloak with your directory or identity provider
guides.audience: Super Admins and User Admins connecting sign-in to the organisation's directory
guides.purpose: Signing people in with the organisation's own accounts: Keycloak with Active Directory or LDAP, Microsoft Entra ID, Google, or any other OpenID Connect or SAML provider; and mapping directory groups to EA Explorer's roles.

guides.title: Security best practice guide
guides.audience: Super Admins, IT Admins and security reviewers
guides.purpose: Keeping an EA Explorer installation secure: the hardening checklist, secrets and certificates, who may reach it, multi-factor sign-in, machine access, and reporting a security issue.

guides.title: Error code guide
guides.audience: IT Admins, Super Admins and anyone who is shown an error code
guides.purpose: Every error code EA Explorer gives (EAX-AREA-NNN): where the codes show, how to look one up from the screens, the machine and Jenkins, and for each code what it means, its usual cause and what to do.

guides.title: Security and performance testing guide
guides.audience: Super Admins and IT Admins who test that EA Explorer is safe and quick, and developers who fix what they find
guides.purpose: The four tests that check EA Explorer is safe and quick: the security suite, the attack test that tries to break it with tools kept up to date, the SonarQube scan of the code, and the benchmark under load; how to run each, read its results, fix or accept a finding in writing, and run it again.
